[2026-10-22T20:30:18.249Z] [INFO]       "content": "# CRISPR-Based Autologous Gene Therapy: Editing a Patient’s Own Cells\n\n**Published:** May 1, 2025  \n**Re-verified:** October 22, 2026 (issue [#7](https://github.com/konard/immortality/issues/7))  \n**Format:** Markdown (for GitHub)\n\n> **Corrections (October 2026).** This document was re-checked against regulator notices,\n> ClinicalTrials.gov records, peer-reviewed trial reports and company SEC filings. The\n> evidence, with a verdict for every claim, is in\n> [docs/case-studies/issue-7/science-verification.md](docs/case-studies/issue-7/science-verification.md).\n> The main changes:\n> - Casgevy does **not** insert a corrected DNA template. It disrupts the *BCL11A* erythroid\n>   enhancer with a single Cas9 cut.\n> - No virus is involved, so “infect” was wrong.\n> - The ClinicalTrials.gov number was mislabelled.\n> - The EDIT-101 method and status were corrected, and the NTLA-2001 status was updated\n>   (Phase 3 clinical hold, then lifted).\n> - The UK figures were split into the two separate NICE decisions.\n\n---\n\n## Introduction\n\nCRISPR–Cas9 and its derivative technologies (base editors, prime editors) have ushered in a\nnew era of precision gene therapy.\n\nIn the **ex vivo** approach:\n- A patient’s own blood stem cells are collected and edited outside the body.\n- The cells are reinfused after chemotherapy conditioning.\n\nThe first approved CRISPR medicine, **Casgevy**, does not insert a corrected gene. It uses a\nsingle Cas9 cut to switch off the *BCL11A* erythroid enhancer, so red cells make fetal\nhaemoglobin again [6, 7, 8].\n\n**In vivo** approaches instead deliver the editor directly into the body, for example by\nlipid nanoparticles to the liver [20, 21].\n\n---\n\n## Mechanism of Action\n\n1. **Targeted DNA Break**  \n   - A guide RNA directs Cas9 (or a Cas variant) to a specific genomic locus, where it makes\n     a double-strand break.\n   - Cells repair this via non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) or homology-directed repair\n     (HDR).\n\n2. **Homology-Directed Repair (HDR)**  \n   - When a donor DNA template with homology arms is provided, the cell’s repair machinery\n     copies in the corrected sequence at the break site.\n\n3. **Base & Prime Editing**  \n   - **Base editors** convert single bases (e.g. A→G or C→T) without double-strand breaks.\n   - **Prime editors** nick one DNA strand and reverse-transcribe the edit from an extended\n     guide RNA (pegRNA), avoiding double-strand breaks.\n\nIn the clinic, most approved or late-stage CRISPR therapies use **NHEJ gene disruption**\nrather than HDR correction: Casgevy, EDIT-101 and NTLA-2001 all work without a donor\ntemplate [6, 18, 20].\n\nTwo newer approaches have each been reported in only one or two patients. Neither has been\nreplicated yet.\n- **In vivo base editing:** a personalised base editor was given to one infant with CPS1\n  deficiency in 2025 [27, 28].\n- **Prime editing:** the first patient data came in 2025, from two patients with p47phox\n  chronic granulomatous disease [29].\n\n[Learn more about HDR, base editing, and prime editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_editing).\n\n---\n\n## Delivery Approaches\n\n| Approach | Description | Examples |\n|----------|-------------|----------|\n| **Ex vivo** | Harvest patient cells (e.g. hematopoietic stem cells) and edit them in culture. For Casgevy this means electroporation of Cas9–guide RNA complexes; some other products use viral vectors. Then reinfuse after conditioning. | CTX001/Casgevy for sickle cell & β-thalassemia |\n| **In vivo** | Direct delivery of editors into the body, e.g. intravenous lipid nanoparticles (NTLA-2001) or subretinal AAV injection (EDIT-101). | EDIT-101 (retina) • NTLA-2001 (liver) |\n\n---\n\n## Clinical Implementations\n\n### Ex vivo Therapy: CTX001 / Casgevy  \n- **Active Ingredient:** Exagamglogene autotemcel (exa-cel, CTX001; brand name **Casgevy**;\n  Vertex / CRISPR Therapeutics)\n- **Indications:**  \n  - Sickle cell disease (SCD) with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises  \n  - Transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia (TDT)  \n- **Mechanism:**\n  - CRISPR–Cas9 cuts a GATA1 binding site in the erythroid-specific enhancer of *BCL11A*.\n  - The cut is repaired by NHEJ, which reactivates fetal hemoglobin (HbF).\n  - The disease-causing *HBB* mutation itself is not corrected [6, 7, 8].\n- **Approval & Rollout:**  \n  - **MHRA (UK):** conditional authorisation 16 November 2023 (world first; ages 12+) [2]\n  - **FDA (US):**\n    - SCD approved 8 December 2023, the same day as bluebird bio’s lentiviral Lyfgenia [1]\n    - TDT approved 16 January 2024 [5]\n    - Label expanded to patients aged 2 years and older in July 2026 [11, 12]\n  - **EU:** conditional marketing authorisation 9 February 2024 [3]\n  - **Worldwide:** approved in 39 countries by mid-2026 [11]\n- **Pivotal trials:**\n  - CLIMB-121 (SCD, [NCT03745287](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03745287))\n  - CLIMB-111 (TDT, [NCT03655678](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03655678))\n  - The results were published in NEJM in 2024 [7, 8].\n- **Paediatric trials:** CLIMB-151 ([NCT05329649](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05329649))\n  and CLIMB-141 ([NCT05356195](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05356195)) supported the\n  2026 label expansion [13].\n\n### In vivo Therapy: EDIT-101  \n- **Indication:** Leber congenital amaurosis 10 (LCA10, *CEP290* IVS26 mutation)\n- **Method:**\n  - An AAV5 vector carries SaCas9 and two guide RNAs, given by subretinal injection.\n  - The guides cut out the IVS26 splice mutation.\n  - There is no donor template [18].\n- **Status:**\n  - Phase 1/2 BRILLIANCE trial ([NCT03872479](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03872479)).\n  - Results in 14 participants were published in NEJM in 2024 (Pierce et al.): safety was\n    acceptable, and only a minority improved [18].\n  - Editas paused the programme in November 2022 to seek a partner [19].\n  - No further development has been announced.\n\n### In vivo Therapy: NTLA-2001 (nexiguran ziclumeran, “nex-z”; Intellia/Regeneron)\n- **Indication:** Transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis, in two forms:\n  - hereditary polyneuropathy (ATTRv-PN)\n  - cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), hereditary or wild-type [20, 21]\n- **Method:**\n  - Lipid nanoparticles deliver Cas9 mRNA and a guide RNA to the liver.\n  - *TTR* is knocked out via NHEJ, with no donor template.\n- **Key Data:**\n  - The Phase 1 trial ([NCT04601051](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04601051)) had\n    72 participants.\n  - A single infusion lowered serum TTR by about 90% on average [20, 21].\n  - The reduction was sustained for at least 1–2 years [21, 22a].\n  - Clinical-outcome benefit is not yet proven.\n- **Status:**\n  - Two Phase 3 trials: MAGNITUDE (ATTR-CM,\n    [NCT06128629](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06128629)) and MAGNITUDE-2 (ATTRv-PN,\n    [NCT06672237](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06672237)).\n  - In October 2025 the FDA placed both on clinical hold after a Grade 4 liver-injury event.\n    The patient later died [22].\n  - The holds were lifted with added liver monitoring: MAGNITUDE-2 in January 2026 and\n    MAGNITUDE in March 2026 [23, 24, 25].\n  - Enrollment has resumed [26].\n\n**No in vivo CRISPR therapy is approved yet (October 2026).** Intellia’s lonvo-z (NTLA-2002,\nhereditary angioedema) reported positive Phase 3 data. Intellia expects a US launch in 2027,\nif the drug is approved [26].\n\n---\n\n## Practical Usage in Patients\n\n- **CTX001/Casgevy** is **commercially available** in 39 countries by mid-2026, including the\n  US, UK, EU, Canada, Switzerland and Gulf states [11].\n  - It is given at authorised treatment centres; there were more than 75 by mid-2025 [9].\n  - It requires myeloablative busulfan conditioning (chemotherapy) before reinfusion. This\n    is the main toxicity and a key barrier to uptake [7, 8].\n  - Patients typically remain hospitalized for several weeks. Neutrophil engraftment took a\n    median of about 4 weeks in the pivotal trials [7, 8].\n  - Uptake is still small relative to need:\n    - 64 patients were infused worldwide in 2025, against an estimated more than 60,000\n      eligible patients [10].\n    - Infusions accelerated in 2026 [11].\n\n- **EDIT-101** and **NTLA-2001** are **not approved**.\n  - EDIT-101 is paused.\n  - NTLA-2001 is in Phase 3 trials at specialised centres.\n\n---\n\n## Cost of Therapy\n\n### United States  \n- **Casgevy list price:** \\$2.2 million USD per one-time treatment [17]. For comparison,\n  Lyfgenia, approved the same day, lists at \\$3.1 million [16].\n- **Payment models:** the following were not individually verified:\n  - Specialty pharmacy hubs  \n  - Outcomes-based agreements  \n  - Installment plans with pay-for-performance clauses  \n\n> Source: [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/crispr-sickle-cell-price-millions-gene-therapy-vertex/702066/)\n\n### United Kingdom (England)\n- **Transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia** [14]:\n  - NICE recommended it in August 2024 via the Innovative Medicines Fund.\n  - The list price is £1.65 million per patient, with a confidential discount.\n  - About 460 patients aged 12+ in England are eligible.\n  - Treatment is given at seven NHS specialist centres.\n- **Sickle cell disease** [15]:\n  - NICE initially rejected it (March 2024).\n  - NICE then recommended it in January 2025 under a managed-access agreement, at the same\n    list price with a confidential discount.\n  - About 50 patients a year are expected to be treated initially.\n\n> Sources: [NHS England, Aug 2024](https://www.england.nhs.uk/2024/08/gene-editing-therapy-that-could-cure-blood-disorder-thalassaemia-for-nhs-patients/); [Pharmaceutical Technology, Jan 2025](https://www.pharmaceutical-technology.com/news/nhs-england-to-offer-casgevy-for-sickle-cell-disease-patients/)\n\n---\n\n## Future Directions\n\n1. **Improving HDR efficiency** in non-dividing cells  \n2. **Next-gen editors** (base and prime editors) with reduced off-target activity  \n3. **Non-viral delivery platforms** (LNPs, nanoparticles) to broaden tissue targeting. LNP\n   delivery to the liver is already in Phase 3 [20, 21, 26]; other tissues remain the\n   challenge.\n4. **Gentler conditioning** than busulfan, so that ex vivo therapies become less toxic\n5. **Cost reduction** through manufacturing scale-up and platform optimization  \n\n---\n\n## Conclusion\n\nCRISPR-based therapies are a real clinical advance for some single-gene diseases.\n**Casgevy** (US list price \\$2.2 million) is approved in dozens of countries, and in vivo\neditors delivered by lipid nanoparticles are in Phase 3.\n\nThey also have clear limits:\n- They remain expensive and demanding: Casgevy requires chemotherapy conditioning.\n- Uptake is still small.\n- Serious adverse events have occurred in trials.\n- None of these therapies targets aging itself.\n\nTreatment with one’s own edited cells is now a reality, but it is a therapy for specific\ndiseases, not a route to immortality.\n\n---\n\n## References\n\n1. Then reinfuse after conditioning. | CTX001/Casgevy for sickle cell & β-thalassemia |\n| **In vivo** | Direct delivery of editors into the body, e.g. intravenous lipid nanoparticles (NTLA-2001) or subretinal AAV injection (EDIT-101). | EDIT-101 (retina) • NTLA-2001 (liver) |\n\n---\n\n## Clinical Implementations\n\n### Ex vivo Therapy: CTX001 / Casgevy  \n- **Active Ingredient:** Exagamglogene autotemcel (exa-cel, CTX001; brand name **Casgevy**;\n  Vertex / CRISPR Therapeutics)\n- **Indications:**  \n  - Sickle cell disease (SCD) with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises  \n  - Transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia (TDT)  \n- **Mechanism:**\n  - CRISPR–Cas9 cuts a GATA1 binding site in the erythroid-specific enhancer of *BCL11A*.\n  - The cut is repaired by NHEJ, which reactivates fetal hemoglobin (HbF).\n  - The disease-causing *HBB* mutation itself is not corrected [6, 7, 8].\n- **Approval & Rollout:**  \n  - **MHRA (UK):** conditional authorisation 16 November 2023 (world first; ages 12+) [2]\n  - **FDA (US):**\n    - SCD approved 8 December 2023, the same day as bluebird bio’s lentiviral Lyfgenia [1]\n    - TDT approved 16 January 2024 [5]\n    - Label expanded to patients aged 2 years and older in July 2026 [11, 12]\n  - **EU:** conditional marketing authorisation 9 February 2024 [3]\n  - **Worldwide:** approved in 39 countries by mid-2026 [11]\n- **Pivotal trials:**\n  - CLIMB-121 (SCD, [NCT03745287](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03745287))\n  - CLIMB-111 (TDT, [NCT03655678](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03655678))\n  - The results were published in NEJM in 2024 [7, 8].\n- **Paediatric trials:** CLIMB-151 ([NCT05329649](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05329649))\n  and CLIMB-141 ([NCT05356195](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05356195)) supported the\n  2026 label expansion [13].\n\n### In vivo Therapy: EDIT-101  \n- **Indication:** Leber congenital amaurosis 10 (LCA10, *CEP290* IVS26 mutation)\n- **Method:**\n  - An AAV5 vector carries SaCas9 and two guide RNAs, given by subretinal injection.\n  - The guides cut out the IVS26 splice mutation.\n  - There is no donor template [18].\n- **Status:**\n  - Phase 1/2 BRILLIANCE trial ([NCT03872479](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03872479)).\n  - Results in 14 participants were published in NEJM in 2024 (Pierce et al.): safety was\n    acceptable, and only a minority improved [18].\n  - Editas paused the programme in November 2022 to seek a partner [19].\n  - No further development has been announced.\n\n### In vivo Therapy: NTLA-2001 (nexiguran ziclumeran, “nex-z”; Intellia/Regeneron)\n- **Indication:** Transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis, in two forms:\n  - hereditary polyneuropathy (ATTRv-PN)\n  - cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), hereditary or wild-type [20, 21]\n- **Method:**\n  - Lipid nanoparticles deliver Cas9 mRNA and a guide RNA to the liver.\n  - *TTR* is knocked out via NHEJ, with no donor template.\n- **Key Data:**\n  - The Phase 1 trial ([NCT04601051](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04601051)) had\n    72 participants.\n  - A single infusion lowered serum TTR by about 90% on average [20, 21].\n  - The reduction was sustained for at least 1–2 years [21, 22a].\n  - Clinical-outcome benefit is not yet proven.\n- **Status:**\n  - Two Phase 3 trials: MAGNITUDE (ATTR-CM,\n    [NCT06128629](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06128629)) and MAGNITUDE-2 (ATTRv-PN,\n    [NCT06672237](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06672237)).\n  - In October 2025 the FDA placed both on clinical hold after a Grade 4 liver-injury event.\n    The patient later died [22].\n  - The holds were lifted with added liver monitoring: MAGNITUDE-2 in January 2026 and\n    MAGNITUDE in March 2026 [23, 24, 25].\n  - Enrollment has resumed [26].\n\n**No in vivo CRISPR therapy is approved yet (October 2026).** Intellia’s lonvo-z (NTLA-2002,\nhereditary angioedema) reported positive Phase 3 data. Intellia expects a US launch in 2027,\nif the drug is approved [26].\n\n---\n\n## Practical Usage in Patients\n\n- **CTX001/Casgevy** is **commercially available** in 39 countries by mid-2026, including the\n  US, UK, EU, Canada, Switzerland and Gulf states [11].\n  - It is given at authorised treatment centres; there were more than 75 by mid-2025 [9].\n  - It requires myeloablative busulfan conditioning (chemotherapy) before reinfusion. This\n    is the main toxicity and a key barrier to uptake [7, 8].\n  - Patients typically remain hospitalized for several weeks. Neutrophil engraftment took a\n    median of about 4 weeks in the pivotal trials [7, 8].\n  - Uptake is still small relative to need:\n    - 64 patients were infused worldwide in 2025, against an estimated more than 60,000\n      eligible patients [10].\n    - Infusions accelerated in 2026 [11].\n\n- **EDIT-101** and **NTLA-2001** are **not approved**.\n  - EDIT-101 is paused.\n  - NTLA-2001 is in Phase 3 trials at specialised centres.\n\n---\n\n## Cost of Therapy\n\n### United States  \n- **Casgevy list price:** \\$2.2 million USD per one-time treatment [17]. For comparison,\n  Lyfgenia, approved the same day, lists at \\$3.1 million [16].\n- **Payment models:** the following were not individually verified:\n  - Specialty pharmacy hubs  \n  - Outcomes-based agreements  \n  - Installment plans with pay-for-performance clauses  \n\n> Source: [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/crispr-sickle-cell-price-millions-gene-therapy-vertex/702066/)\n\n### United Kingdom (England)\n- **Transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia** [14]:\n  - NICE recommended it in August 2024 via the Innovative Medicines Fund.\n  - The list price is £1.65 million per patient, with a confidential discount.\n  - About 460 patients aged 12+ in England are eligible.\n  - Treatment is given at seven NHS specialist centres.\n- **Sickle cell disease** [15]:\n  - NICE initially rejected it (March 2024).\n  - NICE then recommended it in January 2025 under a managed-access agreement, at the same\n    list price with a confidential discount.\n  - About 50 patients a year are expected to be treated initially.\n\n> Sources: [NHS England, Aug 2024](https://www.england.nhs.uk/2024/08/gene-editing-therapy-that-could-cure-blood-disorder-thalassaemia-for-nhs-patients/); [Pharmaceutical Technology, Jan 2025](https://www.pharmaceutical-technology.com/news/nhs-england-to-offer-casgevy-for-sickle-cell-disease-patients/)\n\n---\n\n## Future Directions\n\n1. **Improving HDR efficiency** in non-dividing cells  \n2. **Next-gen editors** (base and prime editors) with reduced off-target activity  \n3. **Non-viral delivery platforms** (LNPs, nanoparticles) to broaden tissue targeting. LNP\n   delivery to the liver is already in Phase 3 [20, 21, 26]; other tissues remain the\n   challenge.\n4. **Gentler conditioning** than busulfan, so that ex vivo therapies become less toxic\n5. **Cost reduction** through manufacturing scale-up and platform optimization  \n\n---\n\n## Conclusion\n\nCRISPR-based therapies are a real clinical advance for some single-gene diseases.\n**Casgevy** (US list price \\$2.2 million) is approved in dozens of countries, and in vivo\neditors delivered by lipid nanoparticles are in Phase 3.\n\nThey also have clear limits:\n- They remain expensive and demanding: Casgevy requires chemotherapy conditioning.\n- Uptake is still small.\n- Serious adverse events have occurred in trials.\n- None of these therapies targets aging itself.\n\nTreatment with one’s own edited cells is now a reality, but it is a therapy for specific\ndiseases, not a route to immortality.\n\n---\n\n## References\n\n1. [2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+- **Active Ingredient:** Exagamglogene autotemcel (exa-cel, CTX001; brand name **Casgevy**;",

[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           " - **Indications:**  ",

[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "-- **Mechanism:** CRISPR–Cas9 targets the BCL11A enhancer to reactivate fetal hemoglobin (HbF).  ",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+  - Transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia (TDT)  ",

[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+  - The disease-causing *HBB* mutation itself is not corrected [6, 7, 8].",

[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           " ",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "-- **CTX001/Casgevy** is **commercially available** in the US and UK.  ",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "-  - Administered at accredited transplant centers.  ",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "-  - Requires myeloablative conditioning (chemotherapy) before reinfusion.  ",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "-  - Patients typically remain hospitalized for several weeks.",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+- **CTX001/Casgevy** is **commercially available** in 39 countries by mid-2026, including the",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+  US, UK, EU, Canada, Switzerland and Gulf states [11].",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+  - It is given at authorised treatment centres; there were more than 75 by mid-2025 [9].",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+  - It requires myeloablative busulfan conditioning (chemotherapy) before reinfusion. This",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+    is the main toxicity and a key barrier to uptake [7, 8].",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+  - Patients typically remain hospitalized for several weeks. Neutrophil engraftment took a",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+    median of about 4 weeks in the pivotal trials [7, 8].",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+  - Uptake is still small relative to need:",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+    - 64 patients were infused worldwide in 2025, against an estimated more than 60,000",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+      eligible patients [10].",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+    - Infusions accelerated in 2026 [11].",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           " ",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "-- **EDIT-101** and **NTLA-2001** remain **investigational**; administered in specialized trial centers.",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+- **EDIT-101** and **NTLA-2001** are **not approved**.",

[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           " ",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "-CRISPR-based autologous gene therapies represent a paradigm shift: patients receive their own genetically corrected cells to cure—or significantly ameliorate—their disease.  With **Casgevy** already in clinical practice at a list price near \\$2 million, and multiple in vivo therapies advancing through trials, this technology is poised to transform medicine, making “infecting” oneself with one’s own DNA not just theory, but reality.",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+CRISPR-based therapies are a real clinical advance for some single-gene diseases.",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+**Casgevy** (US list price \\$2.2 million) is approved in dozens of countries, and in vivo",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+editors delivered by lipid nanoparticles are in Phase 3.",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           " ",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+They also have clear limits:",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+- They remain expensive and demanding: Casgevy requires chemotherapy conditioning.",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+- Uptake is still small.",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+- Serious adverse events have occurred in trials.",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+- None of these therapies targets aging itself.",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+Treatment with one’s own edited cells is now a reality, but it is a therapy for specific",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+diseases, not a route to immortality.",
[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]           "+",

[2026-10-22T20:30:18.298Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "# CRISPR-Based Autologous Gene Therapy: Using Your Own DNA to Repair Damaged Cells\n\n**Published:** May 1, 2025  \n**Format:** Markdown (for GitHub)\n\n---\n\n## Introduction\n\nCRISPR–Cas9 and its derivative technologies (base editors, prime editors) have ushered in a new era of precision gene therapy.  By harvesting a patient’s own cells, delivering the editing machinery along with a “corrected” DNA template, and reinfusing the repaired cells, researchers can now **“infect”** humans with their own DNA to fix disease-causing mutations.\n\n---\n\n## Mechanism of Action\n\n1. **Targeted DNA Break**  \n   - A guide RNA directs Cas9 (or a Cas variant) to a specific genomic locus, where it makes a double-strand break.  \n   - Cells repair this via non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) or homology-directed repair (HDR).  \n\n2. **Homology-Directed Repair (HDR)**  \n   - When a donor DNA template with homology arms is provided, the cell’s repair machinery copies in the corrected sequence at the break site.  \n\n3. **Base & Prime Editing**  \n   - **Base editors** convert single bases (e.g. A→G or C→T) without double-strand breaks.  \n   - **Prime editors** reverse-transcribe edits from an extended guide RNA, also avoiding classic breaks.  \n\n[Learn more about HDR, base editing, and prime editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_editing).\n\n---\n\n## Delivery Approaches\n\n| Approach     | Description                                                                                              | Examples                                                                         |\n|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| **Ex vivo**  | Harvest patient cells (e.g. hematopoietic stem cells), edit in culture (electroporation or viral vector), then reinfuse. | CTX001/Casgevy for sickle cell & β-thalassemia                                     |\n| **In vivo**  | Direct infusion of vectors or nanoparticles carrying editors (± donor DNA) into the patient.              | EDIT-101 (retina) • NTLA-2001 (liver)                                              |\n\n---\n\n## Clinical Implementations\n\n### Ex vivo Therapy: CTX001 / Casgevy  \n- **Active Ingredient:** Exagamglogene autotemcel (CTX001; brand name **Casgevy**)  \n- **Indications:**  \n  - Sickle cell disease (SCD) with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises  \n  - Transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia  \n- **Mechanism:** CRISPR–Cas9 targets the BCL11A enhancer to reactivate fetal hemoglobin (HbF).  \n- **Approval & Rollout:**  \n  - **FDA approval:** December 8, 2023 ([press release](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-gene-therapies-treat-patients-sickle-cell-disease))  \n  - **MHRA (UK):** November 16, 2023; NHS rollout at specialist centers  \n  - **ClinicalTrials.gov:** [NCT05329649](https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT05329649)  \n\n### In vivo Therapy: EDIT-101  \n- **Indication:** Leber congenital amaurosis 10 (LCA10)  \n- **Method:** AAV-SaCas9 + guide RNA + donor template via subretinal injection  \n- **Status:** Phase 1/2 trial [NCT03872479](https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03872479)  \n\n### In vivo Therapy: NTLA-2001  \n- **Indication:** Hereditary transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy  \n- **Method:** Lipid nanoparticles deliver Cas9 mRNA + guide RNA; gene knockout via NHEJ  \n- **Key Data:** Single dose yields > 90 % TTR knockdown for 4–6 months  \n- **Status:** Phase 1 [NCT04601051](https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT04601051) → Phase 3 MAGNITUDE trial  \n\n---\n\n## Practical Usage in Patients\n\n- **CTX001/Casgevy** is **commercially available** in the US and UK.  \n  - Administered at accredited transplant centers.  \n  - Requires myeloablative conditioning (chemotherapy) before reinfusion.  \n  - Patients typically remain hospitalized for several weeks.\n\n- **EDIT-101** and **NTLA-2001** remain **investigational**; administered in specialized trial centers.\n\n---\n\n## Cost of Therapy\n\n### United States  \n- **Casgevy list price:** \\$2.2 million USD per one-time treatment  \n- **Payment models:**  \n  - Specialty pharmacy hubs  \n  - Outcomes-based agreements  \n  - Installment plans with pay-for-performance clauses  \n\n> Source: [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/crispr-sickle-cell-price-millions-gene-therapy-vertex/702066/)\n\n### United Kingdom  \n- **NHS list price:** £1.65 million GBP per patient (via Innovative Medicines Fund)  \n- **Coverage:** Confidential discount agreement; up to ~ 460 eligible patients  \n- **Centres:** Seven NHS specialist centres across England  \n\n> Source: [Nature Biotechnology](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-023-02415-8)\n\n---\n\n## Future Directions\n\n1. **Improving HDR efficiency** in non-dividing cells  \n2. **Next-gen editors** with reduced off-target activity  \n3. **Non-viral delivery platforms** (LNPs, nanoparticles) to broaden tissue targeting  \n4. **Cost reduction** through manufacturing scale-up and platform optimization  \n\n---\n\n## Conclusion\n\nCRISPR-based autologous gene therapies represent a paradigm shift: patients receive their own genetically corrected cells to cure—or significantly ameliorate—their disease.  With **Casgevy** already in clinical practice at a list price near \\$2 million, and multiple in vivo therapies advancing through trials, this technology is poised to transform medicine, making “infecting” oneself with one’s own DNA not just theory, but reality.\n\n---\n\n## References\n\n1. FDA Press Release: “FDA Approves First Gene Therapies to Treat Patients with Sickle Cell Disease”  \n   <https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-gene-therapies-treat-patients-sickle-cell-disease>  \n2. Top 15 missing ideas, with implementation sketches\n\nThey are ordered by how directly they answer the issue, then by effort.\n\n1. **Themed, accessible Select** (issue: \"styled dropdowns\"). `Select.tsx` is in progress.\n   - Structure: a WAI-ARIA select-only combobox (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/examples/combobox-select-only/). A button with `role=\"combobox\"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` owns a `ul[role=listbox]` of `li[role=option]` with `aria-selected`. Use `aria-activedescendant` to track the active option.\n   - Keys: arrow keys, Home/End, typeahead, Enter/Space, Escape, and Tab to close.\n   - Look (gridcn): the panel uses the `--surface` background and a 2-4px scanline `repeating-linear-gradient` overlay. Add a corner bracket in `::before`, a chevron with `transform: rotate(180deg)` when open, and an accent glow on the active option.\n   - Sound: `sounds.select()` on commit and `hover` on active change.\n   - Placement: the panel is `position:absolute`. Flip it upward when `getBoundingClientRect().bottom + h > innerHeight`.\n   - Optional progressive enhancement: `@supports (appearance: base-select)` with `::picker(select)`, Chrome 135+ only (https://developer.chrome.com/blog/a-customizable-select). Not enough on its own.\n\n2. **Themed scrollbars**, for the data table and everywhere else.\n\n   ```css\n   * { scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent) transparent; }\n   ::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 10px; height: 10px; }\n   ::-webkit-scrollbar-track { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 92%, var(--accent) 8%); border-left: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 20%, transparent); }\n   ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent) padding-box; border: 2px solid transparent; box-shadow: inset 0 0 6px var(--accent); }\n   ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover { background-color: var(--accent); }\n   ```\n\n   - The `::-webkit-scrollbar` rules are ignored in Chrome 121+ wherever the standard `scrollbar-*` properties apply (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/css-ui/scrollbar-styling). They remain useful for Safari before 26.2 and older Chromium.\n   - Add the ZKN fade mask on the scroll container, gated on overflow: `mask-image: linear-gradient(transparent, #000 1.5rem, #000 calc(100% - 1.5rem), transparent)`.\n\n3. **Table styling, and no expandable-only sections** (issue).\n   - Render the table directly instead of inside `<details>`. Use a sticky `thead` with a 10% accent tint, 10px uppercase letter-spaced headers, row borders at accent 20%, and row hover at accent 8%.\n   - Colour cells by threshold using `data-level=\"ok|warn|bad\"`.\n   - Give Methodology a FrameHeader-style title and show its text directly. If it is long, split it into two columns or use tabs.\n\n4. **Materials plus a transparency slider** (issue: \"transparency, wood, steel\"). This is not in any reference, so it has to be designed here.\n   - Add a `surfaceOpacity` setting (0.2-1) and set `--surface-alpha` from it.\n   - Add surfaces built only from CSS layers:\n     - steel: `repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, #fff1 0 1px, #0001 1px 3px), linear-gradient(180deg, #8a9099, #4a4f57)`;\n     - carbon: two `repeating-linear-gradient(45deg/-45deg)` checker layers;\n     - wood: inline SVG `feTurbulence baseFrequency=\"0.02 0.4\" numOctaves=3` plus `feColorMatrix` to brown, as a data-URI `background-image`, over `linear-gradient` grain;\n     - brushed titanium;\n     - frosted acrylic: glass plus noise.\n   - Mix each with `color-mix(in srgb, <material> calc(var(--surface-alpha)*100%), transparent)`, or put the material on a `::before` layer with `opacity: var(--surface-alpha)`.\n   - Lea Verou's CSS3 Patterns (MIT) has ready-made gradient patterns: https://projects.verou.me/css3patterns/\n\n5. **Sound variety: several variants per event, not named after actions** (issue).\n   - Make each event map to an array of 3-5 synth recipes. Each play picks one at random, avoiding an immediate repeat, and adds ±3% detune and ±10% gain jitter.\n   - Rename the presets to evocative, non-action names (for example \"Quartz\", \"Relay\", \"Ion\", \"Halcyon\").\n   - Higher fidelity:\n     - layered partials (FM: a modulator oscillator into `carrier.frequency`);\n     - a short `ConvolverNode` reverb from a generated decaying-noise impulse;\n     - a `DynamicsCompressorNode` on the master bus;\n     - a `WaveShaperNode` for gentle saturation.\n   - Arwes Bleeps-style categories (interaction .75, transition .5, notification 1, background .25), each with its own volume slider.\n   - Mute when the window loses focus (`muteOnWindowBlur`).\n   - New events: close, error, info, content, assemble, plus a looping type sound while text effects run.\n\n6. **Fix glitchy borders and fog** (issue).\n   - Borders: give FrameShape strokes `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke` as Soul Extract does, round SVG coordinates to `.5` for 1px lines, and redraw on `ResizeObserver` instead of on layout guesses.\n   - Fog (puffs and nebula): draw radial gradients into an offscreen low-resolution canvas, then upscale with `imageSmoothingQuality = 'high'` to avoid banding. Add a little noise dither. Clamp alpha and cap the number of puffs.\n\n7. **Arwes FrameNero, FrameHeader and FrameCircle** as new frame options in `frameGeometry` / `FrameShape.tsx`.\n   - Nero: a background rect plus 4 filled `cornerLength × cornerWidth` L-squares, with a `[0, 1, .5, 1]` opacity flicker on enter.\n   - Header: a horizontal line plus a 4px deco block at the aligned end. Use it for panel titles.\n\n8. **Arwes style helpers as CSS classes:**\n   - `.sep` (styleSeparator): `linear-gradient(to right, var(--accent) .5rem, transparent .5rem .75rem, color-mix(...) .75rem calc(100% - .75rem), transparent ..., var(--accent) calc(100% - .5rem))`, 1px high;\n   - `.steps`: stepped `repeating-linear-gradient` bars;\n   - `.strip`: hazard stripes `repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, var(--warn) 0 6px, transparent 6px 12px)` for warnings.\n\n9. **Blinking cursor for text effects** (Arwes `blink`, glitchy words-blink).\n   - While FxText sequence or decipher runs, append `<span class=\"fx-caret\" aria-hidden>▌</span>`.\n   - Animate it with `@keyframes blink { 50% { opacity: 0 } }` at 250ms `step-end`, and remove it on completion.\n\n10. **Per-element illuminator clipped to the frame.**\n    - On buttons and panels, track the pointer with `--mx`/`--my` from `pointermove` relative to `getBoundingClientRect`.\n    - Paint `radial-gradient(120px at var(--mx) var(--my), color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 25%, transparent), transparent)` on `::after`.\n    - Clip it with `clip-path: polygon(...)` built from the same chamfer as the frame (octagon: `polygon(var(--c) 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - var(--c)), calc(100% - var(--c)) 100%, 0 100%, 0 var(--c))`).\n\n11. **Soul Extract \"rails\" background:**\n    - 1px line rows every 10px at very low alpha;\n    - per 100px column, one random dotted vertical rail with `setLineDash([3, 7])`; per 200px row, one horizontal rail;\n    - the existing circuit lights travelling along the rails;\n    - a radial light at 25%.\n    - Also add \"//\" slanted ticks (two small skewed rects) at the ends of the page-section rails.\n\n12. **Arwes GridLines and richer Dots:**\n    - New `grid-lines` background using `setLineDash([4])` for horizontal lines and solid verticals, distance 30.\n    - Extend `drawDots` with `type: box | circle | cross` (a cross is two 1px rects) and a one-shot reveal from an origin. A dot's alpha ramps once `time × speed > distance(origin)`, with `originInverted` running the reveal from the edges inward.\n    - Optionally stack layers ZKN-style (dots + grid + rain + radial glow).\n\n13. **Richer StatTile** (gridcn stat-card and stats-counter):\n    - an icon box;\n    - a ▲/▼ delta coloured ok or bad;\n    - an inline SVG sparkline polyline under the value;\n    - a count-up animation with rAF easing from 0 to the value over about 900ms, skipped under reduced motion or when motion is off.\n\n14. **ZKN and Arwes navigation chrome:**\n    - notched header/footer via the clip-path above;\n    - a breadcrumb title with a vertical 3px accent bar and a chamfered rule;\n    - nav underline `transform: scaleX(0 → 1)` with `transform-origin: left` over .2s;\n    - « » pager plus octagon tabs if sections become paged.\n\n15. **Audio-reactive background** (glitchy.website).\n    - Route the synth master through an `AnalyserNode` (`fftSize` 512, so 256 bins). Each frame, read `getByteFrequencyData`.\n    - Low bins above a threshold spawn an expanding wavy ring (radius r, plus `sin(θ·k + t) × amp` per vertex).\n    - High bins spawn short-lived particles.\n    - A permanent faint wavy main circle with r = 0.8 × min(w,h).\n    - With synthesised UI sound this only reacts to clicks. Pair it with an optional ambient drone in the \"background\" category at .25 volume, off by default.\n\nSmaller extras:\n\n- Soul Extract blink-in \"fader\" entrance (1 → 0 → 1 opacity at t/3, t/5, t/2) with a fade sound.\n- Arwes `sequence` and `staggerReverse` entrance order options.\n- gridcn custom slider (tick marks, glowing fill, ring thumb) for the volume, speed and opacity controls.\n- gridcn Radar, Reticle, DataStream log, SignalIndicator and Heatmap widgets.\n- Per-panel scanline overlay.\n- Better backgrounds and gradients (issue): layer a radial gradient (Arwes docs: `radial-gradient(#04252B, #001515)` adapted per palette) under every canvas mode, and add a slow conic or mesh gradient option made of 3-4 blurred radial blobs drifting over time.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Pair it with an optional ambient drone in the \"background\" category at .25 volume, off by default.\n\nSmaller extras:\n\n- Soul Extract blink-in \"fader\" entrance (1 → 0 → 1 opacity at t/3, t/5, t/2) with a fade sound.\n- Arwes `sequence` and `staggerReverse` entrance order options.\n- gridcn custom slider (tick marks, glowing fill, ring thumb) for the volume, speed and opacity controls.\n- gridcn Radar, Reticle, DataStream log, SignalIndicator and Heatmap widgets.\n- Per-panel scanline overlay.\n- Better backgrounds and gradients (issue): layer a radial gradient (Arwes docs: `radial-gradient(#04252B, #001515)` adapted per palette) under every canvas mode, and add a slow conic or mesh gradient option made of 3-4 blurred radial blobs drifting over time.\n\n---\n\n## 7. SVG frames are exempt via `isSvgFrameStyle`.\n   - **SVG frames:**\n     - frameShapes.ts `frameGeometry(style, w, h, cut)` returns `{shape, accents[]}`. `SvgFrameStyle = 'octagon'|'kranox'|'nefrex'` and `SVG_FRAME_STYLES` lists them.\n     - FrameShape.tsx renders `.frame-shape-line` (the stroked shape) and `.frame-shape-accent` (stroke var(--neon), width 3, `corner-fade` animation). The material is clipped to the shape.\n   - **Starfield.tsx:**\n     - The canvas has modes; `resize()` builds per-mode data and `draw()` dispatches with `if (mode === …)`.\n     - Helpers: `tint(alpha, color)`, `seededRandom`, `shouldAnimate`, `step`, `clock`, `width` and `height`.\n     - The CSS grid overlay is used for the square and perspective grids.\n   - **sound.ts:**\n     - `playSound(id, gain)` computes pan and detune and calls `playSpec`.\n     - `trigger(event)` calls `chooseSounds`.\n     - `createBus` chains a highshelf, a compressor and a convolver reverb.\n     - The context is suspended on `visibilitychange` hidden, which already covers \"mute on blur\".\n   - **Motion off:** `.motion-off *` sets `animation-duration: 0.001ms`, delay 0s and iteration count 1. `motionAllowed(settings)` is exported from uiContext.\n   - **Licenses:** Soul Extract is GPL-3.0, so its ideas are re-implemented without copying code. thegridcn has no license, so only looks are taken. Non-finite samples are\n * dropped; fewer than two samples give no sparkline. A flat series is drawn mid-height.\n */\nexport function sparkline(values: number[], width: number, height: number): Sparkline | null {\n  const samples = values.filter(Number.isFinite);\n  if (samples.length < 2) return null;\n  const min = Math.min(...samples);\n  const max = Math.max(...samples);\n  const range = max - min;\n  const pad = 2;\n  const points = samples.map((value, i): [number, number] => [\n    fmt((i / (samples.length - 1)) * width),\n    fmt(range === 0 ? height / 2 : pad + (1 - (value - min) / range) * (height - pad * 2)),\n  ]);\n  const line = points.map(([x, y], i) => `${i === 0 ? 'M' : 'L'}${x},${y}`).join(' ');\n  return {\n    line,\n    area: `${line} L${width},${height} L0,${height} Z`,\n    last: points[points.length - 1],\n  };\n}\n\nconst NUMBER = /^([+-]?)(\\d+)(?:\\.(\\d+))?$/;\n\n/**\n * Renders `target` (a plain decimal such as \"73.2\" or \"+0.0123\") part-way through a count-up\n * from `from`, keeping its sign style and decimal places. `progress` runs 0 → 1 and is eased\n * (ease-out cubic). Text that is not a plain number is returned unchanged.\n */\nexport function countUpText(target: string, progress: number, from = 0): string {\n  const match = NUMBER.exec(target);\n  if (!match) return target;\n  const decimals = match[3]?.length ?? 0;\n  const goal = Number(target);\n  const t = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, progress));\n  const eased = 1 - (1 - t) ** 3;\n  const value = from + (goal - from) * eased;\n  const text = (t >= 1 ? goal : value).toFixed(decimals);\n  return match[1] === '+' && !text.startsWith('-') ? Non-finite samples are\n * dropped; fewer than two samples give no sparkline. A flat series is drawn mid-height.\n */\nexport function sparkline(values: number[], width: number, height: number): Sparkline | null {\n  const samples = values.filter(Number.isFinite);\n  if (samples.length < 2) return null;\n  const min = Math.min(...samples);\n  const max = Math.max(...samples);\n  const range = max - min;\n  const pad = 2;\n  const points = samples.map((value, i): [number, number] => [\n    fmt((i / (samples.length - 1)) * width),\n    fmt(range === 0 ? height / 2 : pad + (1 - (value - min) / range) * (height - pad * 2)),\n  ]);\n  const line = points.map(([x, y], i) => `${i === 0 ? 'M' : 'L'}${x},${y}`).join(' ');\n  return {\n    line,\n    area: `${line} L${width},${height} L0,${height} Z`,\n    last: points[points.length - 1],\n  };\n}\n\nconst NUMBER = /^([+-]?)(\\d+)(?:\\.(\\d+))?$/;\n\n/**\n * Renders `target` (a plain decimal such as \"73.2\" or \"+0.0123\") part-way through a count-up\n * from `from`, keeping its sign style and decimal places. `progress` runs 0 → 1 and is eased\n * (ease-out cubic). It then picks the ideas that are still missing and gives an implementation sketch for each, followed by a short library survey.\n\nResearch date: 2026-10-22. Sources were read straight from GitHub (raw files and trees), from npm or bundlephobia, and from a live Playwright render where one was reachable. Anything I could not check directly is listed in \"Unverified\" at the end.\n\nStatus legend:\n\n- **done**: already recreated.\n- **partial**: something similar exists but is noticeably weaker.\n- **missing**: not in the app.\n\n---\n\n## 0. What the app already has\n\nTaken from `app/src/settings.ts` and `app/src/components/*` at commit `ddca4d7`. The working tree also has an in-progress `app/src/components/Select.tsx`.\n\n- **Palettes:** mission, glitchy, amber, monochrome, tron, ares, clu, athena, aphrodite, poseidon, soulextract, matrix.\n- **Canvas backgrounds** (`Starfield.tsx`): stars, square-grid, perspective-grid, galaxy, planet-orbit, star-orbit, asteroids, dots, moving-lines, puffs, circuit, data-rain, nebula.\n  - `dots` is a box lattice lit by a radial wave from the centre.\n  - `circuit` draws traces, endpoint rings and a travelling pulse.\n- **Glow:** none, light, medium, heavy.\n- **Frames:** corners, octagon, kranox, nefrex, lines, underline, hud, plain. These are measured SVGs drawn by `FrameShape.tsx`, with a corner-size slider.\n- **Surfaces:** gradient, glass (`backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(1.3)`), solid, transparent. There is no opacity control and no materials.\n- **Density.**\n- **Meters:** bar, segmented, ring.\n- **Fonts:** system, mono, orbitron, chakra, electrolize, terminal.\n- **Heading case.**\n- **Text effects:** none, decipher, sequence, glitch.\n- **Scanlines:** off, light, medium, heavy.\n- **Toggles:** scan sweep, vignette, flicker, grain noise, global pointer illuminator, HUD status bar (system, sector, data year, UTC clock).\n- **Intros:** none, boot, transmission. Transmission is the user-gesture gate, the equivalent of Soul Extract's \"ENTER\".\n- **Charts:** line, area, glow, step. Grids: solid, dashed, dots, none. LineChart includes a scanner.\n- **Entrances:** assemble, fade, scan, flicker, none. There is a stagger toggle and a speed control.\n- **Sound:** a Web Audio synth (`sound.ts`).\n  - Presets: spark, confirm, transmit, scanner, soft, pulse, typing, deploy, expand, static, silent.\n  - Events: hover, activate, select, scan, open, type, intro.\n  - Master volume control.\n- **Presets and share links:** `#ui=` share hash.\n- **Gaps relevant to the issue:**\n  - Native `<select>` at `App.tsx:254` and `SettingsPanel.tsx:148/366`. Its popup cannot be themed. `Select.tsx` is being added to replace it.\n  - `DataTable` and `Methodology` sections contain nothing but a `<details>`.\n  - No `scrollbar-color` or `::-webkit-scrollbar` rule anywhere in `styles.css`.\n  - `StatTile` shows only label, value, unit and hint.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Top 15 missing ideas, with implementation sketches\n\nThey are ordered by how directly they answer the issue, then by effort.\n\n1. **Themed, accessible Select** (issue: \"styled dropdowns\"). `Select.tsx` is in progress.\n   - Structure: a WAI-ARIA select-only combobox (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/examples/combobox-select-only/). A button with `role=\"combobox\"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` owns a `ul[role=listbox]` of `li[role=option]` with `aria-selected`. Use `aria-activedescendant` to track the active option.\n   - Keys: arrow keys, Home/End, typeahead, Enter/Space, Escape, and Tab to close.\n   - Look (gridcn): the panel uses the `--surface` background and a 2-4px scanline `repeating-linear-gradient` overlay. Add a corner bracket in `::before`, a chevron with `transform: rotate(180deg)` when open, and an accent glow on the active option.\n   - Sound: `sounds.select()` on commit and `hover` on active change.\n   - Placement: the panel is `position:absolute`. Flip it upward when `getBoundingClientRect().bottom + h > innerHeight`.\n   - Optional progressive enhancement: `@supports (appearance: base-select)` with `::picker(select)`, Chrome 135+ only (https://developer.chrome.com/blog/a-customizable-select). Not enough on its own.\n\n2. **Themed scrollbars**, for the data table and everywhere else.\n\n   ```css\n   * { scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent) transparent; }\n   ::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 10px; height: 10px; }\n   ::-webkit-scrollbar-track { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 92%, var(--accent) 8%); border-left: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 20%, transparent); }\n   ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent) padding-box; border: 2px solid transparent; box-shadow: inset 0 0 6px var(--accent); }\n   ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover { background-color: var(--accent); }\n   ```\n\n   - The `::-webkit-scrollbar` rules are ignored in Chrome 121+ wherever the standard `scrollbar-*` properties apply (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/css-ui/scrollbar-styling). They remain useful for Safari before 26.2 and older Chromium.\n   - Add the ZKN fade mask on the scroll container, gated on overflow: `mask-image: linear-gradient(transparent, #000 1.5rem, #000 calc(100% - 1.5rem), transparent)`.\n\n3. **Table styling, and no expandable-only sections** (issue).\n   - Render the table directly instead of inside `<details>`. Use a sticky `thead` with a 10% accent tint, 10px uppercase letter-spaced headers, row borders at accent 20%, and row hover at accent 8%.\n   - Colour cells by threshold using `data-level=\"ok|warn|bad\"`.\n   - Give Methodology a FrameHeader-style title and show its text directly. If it is long, split it into two columns or use tabs.\n\n4. **Materials plus a transparency slider** (issue: \"transparency, wood, steel\"). This is not in any reference, so it has to be designed here.\n   - Add a `surfaceOpacity` setting (0.2-1) and set `--surface-alpha` from it.\n   - Add surfaces built only from CSS layers:\n     - steel: `repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, #fff1 0 1px, #0001 1px 3px), linear-gradient(180deg, #8a9099, #4a4f57)`;\n     - carbon: two `repeating-linear-gradient(45deg/-45deg)` checker layers;\n     - wood: inline SVG `feTurbulence baseFrequency=\"0.02 0.4\" numOctaves=3` plus `feColorMatrix` to brown, as a data-URI `background-image`, over `linear-gradient` grain;\n     - brushed titanium;\n     - frosted acrylic: glass plus noise.\n   - Mix each with `color-mix(in srgb, <material> calc(var(--surface-alpha)*100%), transparent)`, or put the material on a `::before` layer with `opacity: var(--surface-alpha)`.\n   - Lea Verou's CSS3 Patterns (MIT) has ready-made gradient patterns: https://projects.verou.me/css3patterns/\n\n5. **Sound variety: several variants per event, not named after actions** (issue).\n   - Make each event map to an array of 3-5 synth recipes. Each play picks one at random, avoiding an immediate repeat, and adds ±3% detune and ±10% gain jitter.\n   - Rename the presets to evocative, non-action names (for example \"Quartz\", \"Relay\", \"Ion\", \"Halcyon\").\n   - Higher fidelity:\n     - layered partials (FM: a modulator oscillator into `carrier.frequency`);\n     - a short `ConvolverNode` reverb from a generated decaying-noise impulse;\n     - a `DynamicsCompressorNode` on the master bus;\n     - a `WaveShaperNode` for gentle saturation.\n   - Arwes Bleeps-style categories (interaction .75, transition .5, notification 1, background .25), each with its own volume slider.\n   - Mute when the window loses focus (`muteOnWindowBlur`).\n   - New events: close, error, info, content, assemble, plus a looping type sound while text effects run.\n\n6. **Fix glitchy borders and fog** (issue).\n   - Borders: give FrameShape strokes `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke` as Soul Extract does, round SVG coordinates to `.5` for 1px lines, and redraw on `ResizeObserver` instead of on layout guesses.\n   - Fog (puffs and nebula): draw radial gradients into an offscreen low-resolution canvas, then upscale with `imageSmoothingQuality = 'high'` to avoid banding. Add a little noise dither. Clamp alpha and cap the number of puffs.\n\n7. **Arwes FrameNero, FrameHeader and FrameCircle** as new frame options in `frameGeometry` / `FrameShape.tsx`.\n   - Nero: a background rect plus 4 filled `cornerLength × cornerWidth` L-squares, with a `[0, 1, .5, 1]` opacity flicker on enter.\n   - Header: a horizontal line plus a 4px deco block at the aligned end. Use it for panel titles.\n\n8. **Arwes style helpers as CSS classes:**\n   - `.sep` (styleSeparator): `linear-gradient(to right, var(--accent) .5rem, transparent .5rem .75rem, color-mix(...) .75rem calc(100% - .75rem), transparent ..., var(--accent) calc(100% - .5rem))`, 1px high;\n   - `.steps`: stepped `repeating-linear-gradient` bars;\n   - `.strip`: hazard stripes `repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, var(--warn) 0 6px, transparent 6px 12px)` for warnings.\n\n9. **Blinking cursor for text effects** (Arwes `blink`, glitchy words-blink).\n   - While FxText sequence or decipher runs, append `<span class=\"fx-caret\" aria-hidden>▌</span>`.\n   - Animate it with `@keyframes blink { 50% { opacity: 0 } }` at 250ms `step-end`, and remove it on completion.\n\n10. **Per-element illuminator clipped to the frame.**\n    - On buttons and panels, track the pointer with `--mx`/`--my` from `pointermove` relative to `getBoundingClientRect`.\n    - Paint `radial-gradient(120px at var(--mx) var(--my), color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 25%, transparent), transparent)` on `::after`.\n    - Clip it with `clip-path: polygon(...)` built from the same chamfer as the frame (octagon: `polygon(var(--c) 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - var(--c)), calc(100% - var(--c)) 100%, 0 100%, 0 var(--c))`).\n\n11. **Soul Extract \"rails\" background:**\n    - 1px line rows every 10px at very low alpha;\n    - per 100px column, one random dotted vertical rail with `setLineDash([3, 7])`; per 200px row, one horizontal rail;\n    - the existing circuit lights travelling along the rails;\n    - a radial light at 25%.\n    - Also add \"//\" slanted ticks (two small skewed rects) at the ends of the page-section rails.\n\n12. **Arwes GridLines and richer Dots:**\n    - New `grid-lines` background using `setLineDash([4])` for horizontal lines and solid verticals, distance 30.\n    - Extend `drawDots` with `type: box | circle | cross` (a cross is two 1px rects) and a one-shot reveal from an origin. A dot's alpha ramps once `time × speed > distance(origin)`, with `originInverted` running the reveal from the edges inward.\n    - Optionally stack layers ZKN-style (dots + grid + rain + radial glow).\n\n13. **Richer StatTile** (gridcn stat-card and stats-counter):\n    - an icon box;\n    - a ▲/▼ delta coloured ok or bad;\n    - an inline SVG sparkline polyline under the value;\n    - a count-up animation with rAF easing from 0 to the value over about 900ms, skipped under reduced motion or when motion is off.\n\n14. **ZKN and Arwes navigation chrome:**\n    - notched header/footer via the clip-path above;\n    - a breadcrumb title with a vertical 3px accent bar and a chamfered rule;\n    - nav underline `transform: scaleX(0 → 1)` with `transform-origin: left` over .2s;\n    - « » pager plus octagon tabs if sections become paged.\n\n15. **Audio-reactive background** (glitchy.website).\n    - Route the synth master through an `AnalyserNode` (`fftSize` 512, so 256 bins). Each frame, read `getByteFrequencyData`.\n    - Low bins above a threshold spawn an expanding wavy ring (radius r, plus `sin(θ·k + t) × amp` per vertex).\n    - High bins spawn short-lived particles.\n    - A permanent faint wavy main circle with r = 0.8 × min(w,h).\n    - With synthesised UI sound this only reacts to clicks. Pair it with an optional ambient drone in the \"background\" category at .25 volume, off by default.\n\nSmaller extras:\n\n- Soul Extract blink-in \"fader\" entrance (1 → 0 → 1 opacity at t/3, t/5, t/2) with a fade sound.\n- Arwes `sequence` and `staggerReverse` entrance order options.\n- gridcn custom slider (tick marks, glowing fill, ring thumb) for the volume, speed and opacity controls.\n- gridcn Radar, Reticle, DataStream log, SignalIndicator and Heatmap widgets.\n- Per-panel scanline overlay.\n- Better backgrounds and gradients (issue): layer a radial gradient (Arwes docs: `radial-gradient(#04252B, #001515)` adapted per palette) under every canvas mode, and add a slow conic or mesh gradient option made of 3-4 blurred radial blobs drifting over time.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Not enough on its own.\n\n2. **Themed scrollbars**, for the data table and everywhere else.\n\n   ```css\n   * { scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent) transparent; }\n   ::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 10px; height: 10px; }\n   ::-webkit-scrollbar-track { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 92%, var(--accent) 8%); border-left: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 20%, transparent); }\n   ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent) padding-box; border: 2px solid transparent; box-shadow: inset 0 0 6px var(--accent); }\n   ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover { background-color: var(--accent); }\n   ```\n\n   - The `::-webkit-scrollbar` rules are ignored in Chrome 121+ wherever the standard `scrollbar-*` properties apply (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/css-ui/scrollbar-styling). They remain useful for Safari before 26.2 and older Chromium.\n   - Add the ZKN fade mask on the scroll container, gated on overflow: `mask-image: linear-gradient(transparent, #000 1.5rem, #000 calc(100% - 1.5rem), transparent)`.\n\n3. **Table styling, and no expandable-only sections** (issue).\n   - Render the table directly instead of inside `<details>`. Use a sticky `thead` with a 10% accent tint, 10px uppercase letter-spaced headers, row borders at accent 20%, and row hover at accent 8%.\n   - Colour cells by threshold using `data-level=\"ok|warn|bad\"`.\n   - Give Methodology a FrameHeader-style title and show its text directly. If it is long, split it into two columns or use tabs.\n\n4. **Materials plus a transparency slider** (issue: \"transparency, wood, steel\"). This is not in any reference, so it has to be designed here.\n   - Add a `surfaceOpacity` setting (0.2-1) and set `--surface-alpha` from it.\n   - Add surfaces built only from CSS layers:\n     - steel: `repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, #fff1 0 1px, #0001 1px 3px), linear-gradient(180deg, #8a9099, #4a4f57)`;\n     - carbon: two `repeating-linear-gradient(45deg/-45deg)` checker layers;\n     - wood: inline SVG `feTurbulence baseFrequency=\"0.02 0.4\" numOctaves=3` plus `feColorMatrix` to brown, as a data-URI `background-image`, over `linear-gradient` grain;\n     - brushed titanium;\n     - frosted acrylic: glass plus noise.\n   - Mix each with `color-mix(in srgb, <material> calc(var(--surface-alpha)*100%), transparent)`, or put the material on a `::before` layer with `opacity: var(--surface-alpha)`.\n   - Lea Verou's CSS3 Patterns (MIT) has ready-made gradient patterns: https://projects.verou.me/css3patterns/\n\n5. **Sound variety: several variants per event, not named after actions** (issue).\n   - Make each event map to an array of 3-5 synth recipes. Each play picks one at random, avoiding an immediate repeat, and adds ±3% detune and ±10% gain jitter.\n   - Rename the presets to evocative, non-action names (for example \"Quartz\", \"Relay\", \"Ion\", \"Halcyon\").\n   - Higher fidelity:\n     - layered partials (FM: a modulator oscillator into `carrier.frequency`);\n     - a short `ConvolverNode` reverb from a generated decaying-noise impulse;\n     - a `DynamicsCompressorNode` on the master bus;\n     - a `WaveShaperNode` for gentle saturation.\n   - Arwes Bleeps-style categories (interaction .75, transition .5, notification 1, background .25), each with its own volume slider.\n   - Mute when the window loses focus (`muteOnWindowBlur`).\n   - New events: close, error, info, content, assemble, plus a looping type sound while text effects run.\n\n6. **Fix glitchy borders and fog** (issue).\n   - Borders: give FrameShape strokes `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke` as Soul Extract does, round SVG coordinates to `.5` for 1px lines, and redraw on `ResizeObserver` instead of on layout guesses.\n   - Fog (puffs and nebula): draw radial gradients into an offscreen low-resolution canvas, then upscale with `imageSmoothingQuality = 'high'` to avoid banding. Add a little noise dither. Clamp alpha and cap the number of puffs.\n\n7. **Arwes FrameNero, FrameHeader and FrameCircle** as new frame options in `frameGeometry` / `FrameShape.tsx`.\n   - Nero: a background rect plus 4 filled `cornerLength × cornerWidth` L-squares, with a `[0, 1, .5, 1]` opacity flicker on enter.\n   - Header: a horizontal line plus a 4px deco block at the aligned end. Use it for panel titles.\n\n8. **Arwes style helpers as CSS classes:**\n   - `.sep` (styleSeparator): `linear-gradient(to right, var(--accent) .5rem, transparent .5rem .75rem, color-mix(...) .75rem calc(100% - .75rem), transparent ..., var(--accent) calc(100% - .5rem))`, 1px high;\n   - `.steps`: stepped `repeating-linear-gradient` bars;\n   - `.strip`: hazard stripes `repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, var(--warn) 0 6px, transparent 6px 12px)` for warnings.\n\n9. **Blinking cursor for text effects** (Arwes `blink`, glitchy words-blink).\n   - While FxText sequence or decipher runs, append `<span class=\"fx-caret\" aria-hidden>▌</span>`.\n   - Animate it with `@keyframes blink { 50% { opacity: 0 } }` at 250ms `step-end`, and remove it on completion.\n\n10. **Per-element illuminator clipped to the frame.**\n    - On buttons and panels, track the pointer with `--mx`/`--my` from `pointermove` relative to `getBoundingClientRect`.\n    - Paint `radial-gradient(120px at var(--mx) var(--my), color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 25%, transparent), transparent)` on `::after`.\n    - Clip it with `clip-path: polygon(...)` built from the same chamfer as the frame (octagon: `polygon(var(--c) 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - var(--c)), calc(100% - var(--c)) 100%, 0 100%, 0 var(--c))`).\n\n11. **Soul Extract \"rails\" background:**\n    - 1px line rows every 10px at very low alpha;\n    - per 100px column, one random dotted vertical rail with `setLineDash([3, 7])`; per 200px row, one horizontal rail;\n    - the existing circuit lights travelling along the rails;\n    - a radial light at 25%.\n    - Also add \"//\" slanted ticks (two small skewed rects) at the ends of the page-section rails.\n\n12. **Arwes GridLines and richer Dots:**\n    - New `grid-lines` background using `setLineDash([4])` for horizontal lines and solid verticals, distance 30.\n    - Extend `drawDots` with `type: box | circle | cross` (a cross is two 1px rects) and a one-shot reveal from an origin. A dot's alpha ramps once `time × speed > distance(origin)`, with `originInverted` running the reveal from the edges inward.\n    - Optionally stack layers ZKN-style (dots + grid + rain + radial glow).\n\n13. **Richer StatTile** (gridcn stat-card and stats-counter):\n    - an icon box;\n    - a ▲/▼ delta coloured ok or bad;\n    - an inline SVG sparkline polyline under the value;\n    - a count-up animation with rAF easing from 0 to the value over about 900ms, skipped under reduced motion or when motion is off.\n\n14. **ZKN and Arwes navigation chrome:**\n    - notched header/footer via the clip-path above;\n    - a breadcrumb title with a vertical 3px accent bar and a chamfered rule;\n    - nav underline `transform: scaleX(0 → 1)` with `transform-origin: left` over .2s;\n    - « » pager plus octagon tabs if sections become paged.\n\n15. **Audio-reactive background** (glitchy.website).\n    - Route the synth master through an `AnalyserNode` (`fftSize` 512, so 256 bins). Each frame, read `getByteFrequencyData`.\n    - Low bins above a threshold spawn an expanding wavy ring (radius r, plus `sin(θ·k + t) × amp` per vertex).\n    - High bins spawn short-lived particles.\n    - A permanent faint wavy main circle with r = 0.8 × min(w,h).\n    - With synthesised UI sound this only reacts to clicks. Pair it with an optional ambient drone in the \"background\" category at .25 volume, off by default.\n\nSmaller extras:\n\n- Soul Extract blink-in \"fader\" entrance (1 → 0 → 1 opacity at t/3, t/5, t/2) with a fade sound.\n- Arwes `sequence` and `staggerReverse` entrance order options.\n- gridcn custom slider (tick marks, glowing fill, ring thumb) for the volume, speed and opacity controls.\n- gridcn Radar, Reticle, DataStream log, SignalIndicator and Heatmap widgets.\n- Per-panel scanline overlay.\n- Better backgrounds and gradients (issue): layer a radial gradient (Arwes docs: `radial-gradient(#04252B, #001515)` adapted per palette) under every canvas mode, and add a slow conic or mesh gradient option made of 3-4 blurred radial blobs drifting over time.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Summary\n\nThis PR rechecks every scientific conclusion in the repository against current primary sources, using a multi-group consensus rule. It also makes the issue's configuration the default UI and reworks the UI so that every element, material and sound is part of the skin. The full case study, which maps every sentence of the issue to its implementation and evidence, is in [`docs/case-studies/issue-7/`](https://github.com/konard/immortality/tree/issue-7-9ac8b35f1223/docs/case-studies/issue-7).\n\n### Science\n- **Re-verification of every claim** ([`science-verification.md`](https://github.com/konard/immortality/blob/issue-7-9ac8b35f1223/docs/case-studies/issue-7/science-verification.md)). This covers `CRISPR-Autologous-Gene-Therapy.md`, the dashboard verdict and methodology text, and the LEV metric.\n  - **Sources:** 108 numbered references: FDA, MHRA, EMA and NICE notices, ClinicalTrials.gov (API v2), SEC 8-K filings and peer-reviewed papers. Every journal DOI was resolved through Crossref.\n  - **Verdicts:** each claim gets one of Confirmed, Corrected, Outdated, Unconfirmed-single-study or Speculative.\n  - **Consensus rule:** a conclusion is called *likely* only when independent groups, ideally in different countries, agree. Single-study results are labelled as such, and items that could not be verified are listed instead of being assumed.\n- **Corrections in `CRISPR-Autologous-Gene-Therapy.md`:**\n  - Casgevy disrupts the *BCL11A* enhancer instead of inserting a corrected template.\n  - No virus is involved, so \"infect\" was wrong.\n  - The trial number was mislabelled.\n  - The EDIT-101 method and status were wrong.\n  - The NTLA-2001 Phase 3 clinical hold, and its lifting, are now included.\n  - The UK figures are split into the two separate NICE decisions.\n- **Dashboard text:**\n  - LEV is now presented as a *proxy*, meaning period life expectancy rising by 1 year per year. It is not de Grey's actuarial definition, and the text calls it a speculative hypothesis rather than a consensus.\n  - Velocity peaks are no longer explained with one hard-coded story for every country.\n  - The verdict now cites multi-group forecasts (UN WPP 2024, GBD 2021, Oeppen & Vaupel 2002, Vaupel et al. 2021).\n  - The text states that no therapy is approved to slow or reverse aging.\n\n### UI and UX\n- **Default look:** exactly the issue's configuration (Poseidon, medium glow, transparent, spacious, segmented, Orbitron, typewriter, horizon grid, status bar, boot intro, area chart, dashed grid, scan entrance, stagger). Saved settings and share links from the first release migrate correctly.\n- **Materials:** 13 materials (main had 4): gradient, glass, frosted, flat, transparent, brushed steel, brass, copper, walnut wood, carbon fibre, holographic, black marble and concrete. Every material has configurable **opacity** and **backdrop blur**. They are built only from CSS gradients and SVG noise, with no image assets.\n- **Every element is skinned:**\n  - **Dropdowns:** a new WAI-ARIA select-only combobox replaces native selects. It supports keyboard navigation and type-ahead, flips up near the bottom of the viewport, and plays sounds.\n  - **Data table:** four styles (lined, zebra, grid, terminal) with a sticky header.\n  - **Scrollbars:** three styles (thin, HUD rail, block).\n  - **Other controls:** sliders, toggles, tabs and focus rings all take the skin.\n  - **Regression test:** a test requires a CSS rule for every option of every visual axis.\n- **Sounds:** a library of 26 synthesized sounds with neutral names (Quartz, Cobalt, Tungsten, Opal, Sonar, …).\n  - Each of 10 interactions can map to **several** sounds, played at random (never repeating the last pick), in turn, or layered.\n  - The master bus adds a tone shelf, a compressor/limiter, convolution reverb, pitch variation and pointer-positioned stereo.\n  - Every sound was rendered offline: none clips (highest peak 0.895) and none is silent.\n- **More configuration:** 49 axes (main had 28) and 12 presets (main had 8), including Foundry (steel and brass), Study (walnut) and Resonance.\n- **Backgrounds:** 21 backgrounds (main had 13), adding aurora curtains, warp drive, hex lattice, radar sweep, constellation network, Arwes grid lines, Soul Extract signal rails and a sound-resonance ring. There are also 6 backdrop gradients and intensity and speed sliders.\n- **Reference ideas not yet recreated:** all 15 from the new survey were addressed, and three are partial. Added:\n  - the Arwes Nero frame;\n  - title decorations (Arwes rule, zknet bar, Soul Extract `//`);\n  - section dividers (Arwes separator, steps and hazard strip);\n  - a typewriter caret;\n  - stat-card sparklines and counting numbers;\n  - a resonance background driven by interface sound cues.\n\n  The partial items:\n  - **FrameCircle:** not added, because every panel is rectangular.\n  - **Stat-card icon box:** not added.\n  - **Navigation chrome:** the pager, tabs and nav underline don't apply, because the app has no navigation. Only the \"Accent bar\" title decoration came from it.\n- **No expandable-only sections:** Methodology and the data table show their full content.\n- **Glitch fixes:**\n  - **Panel borders:** entrance animations used `fill-mode: both`, which left `clip-path` and transforms on finished panels. That was the root cause.\n  - **\"Fog\" that appeared and disappeared:** the flicker overlay flashed white with `steps(1)` keyframes. It now breathes smoothly.\n  - **Settings drawer:** its corners are pinned to the viewport.\n\n| Default (Poseidon) | Materials |\n| --- | --- |\n|
